{{nihongo|'''Ifuribe Shrine'''|伊富利部神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Ichinomiya, Aichi|Q270810|qid=Q270810}}, {{ill|Aichi Prefecture|Q80434|qid=Q80434}} (former {{ill|Kisogawa, Aichi|Q6416838|qid=Q6416838}} in {{ill|Haguri District|Q1032507|qid=Q1032507}}). Its former {{ill|Shakaku|Q10444029|qid=Q10444029}} was kensha. It is also called '''Ifuribe Shrine''' with a variant character. It is identified with "Ifuribe Shrine" of Haguri District, {{ill|Owari Province|Q514506|qid=Q514506}}, in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Shikinaisha register}}. {{nihongo|'''Ifuribe Shrine'''|伊富利部神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Owari Province]].

==Enshrined deities==
; Main deity
* {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Wakatsuho-no-Mikoto}} (ワカツホノミコト) - descendant of {{ill|Amenohoakari|Q10940411|qid=Q10940411}}, said to be a deity related to metal smelting.

; Associated deity
* {{ill|Hachiman|ar|الإمبراطور أوجين|arz|الامبراطور اوجين|azb|اوجین (ایمپیراتور)|bn|সম্রাট ওজিন|cs|Ódžin|de|Ōjin|es|Ōjin Tennō|eu|Ōjin enperadorea|fa|امپراتور اوجین|fi|Ōjin|fr|Ōjin|hr|Ōjin|id|Kaisar Ōjin|it|Ōjin|ja|応神天皇|ka|ოძინი|ko|오진 천황|nl|Ojin|pl|Ōjin|pt|Ojin|ru|Император Одзин|sh|Car Ōjin|simple|Emperor Ōjin|sl|Cesar Odžin|sv|Ojin|th|จักรพรรดิโอจิง|tl|Emperador Ōjin|tr|Ōjin (imparator)|uk|Імператор Одзін|uz|Imperator Ōjin|vi|Thiên hoàng Ōjin|yo|Emperor Ōjin|zh|应神天皇|zh_min_nan|Ôzin Thian-hông|zh_yue|應神天皇|qid=Q317997|lt=Hondawake-no-Mikoto}} (ホンダワケノミコト)

== History ==
This shrine is related to the Ifuribe clan (Ifukibe clan). One theory says the Ifuribe clan moved from {{ill|Mount Katsuragi|Q11620894|qid=Q11620894}} in {{ill|Yamato Province|Q907495|qid=Q907495}} to this area of Owari and enshrined their ancestors. In the {{ill|Jinshin War|Q2378252|qid=Q2378252}} of {{ill|672|Q30601|qid=Q30601}}, the Ifuribe clan of Owari supported {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|Q335181|qid=Q335181|lt=Prince Ōama}}, so Ifuribe Shrine is inferred to predate that war.

From late {{ill|Heian period|Q193292|qid=Q193292}} onward, under influence of Hachiman faith, Hondawake-no-Mikoto was merged and the name was changed to Shō Hachimangū.
